newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Key facts about the West Bank.
newsitem.headline: Key facts about the West Bank.

text.p: A deal wrapped up on Wednesday commits Israel to hand over most of the West Bank town of Hebron to Palestinian self-rule within 10 days and largely rural parts of the territory by mid-1998.

Here are key facts about the West Bank, which Israel captured in the 1967 Middle East war from Jordan and has begun handing over to Palestinians under peace deals with the Palestine Liberation Organisation.
POPULATION: 1.2 million (Palestinian estimate). About 130,000 Jews live in settlements, excluding East Jerusalem (Western estimates; settlers put their number at more than 140,000).
GDP: Palestinian Monetary Authority estimated 1996 GDP for West Bank and Gaza Strip at $1.856 billion at current prices or $1.633 billion according to 1995 prices. Per capita GDP $652.
RELIGION: 97 percent Moslem, three percent Christian.
MODERN HISTORY: In 1947, the United Nations General Assembly voted to partition the territory of British mandatory Palestine into a Jewish state and an Arab state.
Rejecting the partition, neighbouring Arab states sent troops to prevent the setting up of a Jewish state in Palestine after Britain withdrew its forces in May 1948.

By the end of the war between the Arab and Jewish forces, mandatory Palestine was divided into three territories: the Jewish state of Israel, the West Bank under Jordanian control and the Gaza Strip under Egyptian control.
Israel occupied the West Bank and Gaza in the 1967 Middle East war and established military rule there.
In December 1987, the "intifada" or Palestinian popular uprising against Israeli rule erupted in Gaza's Jabalya refugee camp, quickly spreading throughout the occupied territories.
Television footage of stone-throwing Palestinian children confronting Israeli soldiers on the streets captured world attention.
The Palestine Liberation Organisation is the leading political force in the West Bank and Gaza. The Hamas Islamic Resistance Movement is also a powerful political group.
In September 1993, the Israeli government recognised the PLO, previously branded a "terrorist group", after signing a broad agreement for self-rule.

The peace accord was sealed in another agreement on May 4, 1994, under which Israel withdrew its forces from most of the Gaza Strip and from the West Bank town of Jericho, launching the first stage of a five-year interim Palestinian self-rule.

Another agreement was signed in September 1995 to expand Palestinian self-rule to seven West Bank towns. In six towns, the handover took place within months. The handover of Hebron, the seventh town, was held up by security concerns, violence and a change of government in Israel.

Israel and the PLO have agreed to expand self-rule further by mid-1998 while negotiating the final status of all of the occupied teritories, including the thorny subject of Arab East Jerusalem and the fate of Jewish settlers.
